Which county bills a Portland house

Multnomah County bills most Portland addresses. Portland covers about 145 square miles, and a few slivers reach into Clackamas and Washington counties. Own a house in one of those slivers? Phone that county to learn who bills you, since everything below describes Multnomah accounts only.

An estimated 635,109 people lived in the city in mid-2025. Owners occupy 52.0% of homes, and a median owner-occupied home was valued at $581,500 for 2020 to 2024. Measurable precipitation falls on about 157 days a year, so buyers start their inspection at the roof and drainage. The June 2021 heat wave, which set a 116 degree record, also made people look harder at older houses.

Location, transit and neighborhoods

Distance to a MAX stop or a freeway can count as much as the house itself. TriMet operates most regional buses and the five MAX lines. Interstate 5 runs north-south, I-405 circles downtown, I-205 arcs through the east side to the airport, and I-84 heads for Boise. The airport is 20 minutes from downtown by car, or 40 by MAX.

East and west are split by the Willamette, north and south by Burnside. Since South Portland joined in 2020, an address belongs to one of six sectors: N, NE, NW, S, SE or SW. There are 95 recognized neighborhoods, each with a volunteer association, and as of January 1, 2025 a mayor and a 12-member council elected from four districts run the city.

Multnomah County tax dates for Portland owners

Two deadlines matter this year: payment on November 16, 2026 and appeals by December 31, 2026. Values reflect January 1, 2026. Roughly 300,000 statements and value notices went out, and owners should have had theirs by November 1.

DateWhat happens
January 1, 2026Value date for the 2026 tax roll
November 16, 2026First payment due; 3% discount for full payment, 2% for two-thirds
December 31, 2026Last day for a value appeal, by USPS postmark or delivery
February 16, 2027Second installment due on the three-payment plan
First Monday in February to April 15Appeals hearings
May 17, 2027Third installment due

State law fixes the due date. The county has no power to extend it or forgive late interest.

How to pay

There are five ways to pay: online, phone, mail, a drop box open around the clock, or the counter at the Multnomah Building, 501 SE Hawthorne Blvd. The proptax.multco.us site can draw straight from a bank account, though convenience fees apply.

  • Phone: 503-988-2225, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Counter: Suite 175, same weekday hours.
  • Mail: P.O. Box 2716, Portland, OR 97208-2716, with a postmark no later than the due date.
  • Drop box: checks only.

Taxes across all districts in Multnomah County total $2.602 billion for 2026, up about 3.5% from $2.515 billion in 2025. If a payment has not processed by December 1, call customer service.

A yellow statement signals that a mortgage lender or similar party asked for the bill. Confirm with them first so the same installment is not paid twice.

Reading your statement

Two values appear: real market value (the assessor's January 1 estimate) and assessed value (the smaller of that and maximum assessed value). Every taxing district on the bill charges a permanent rate for ongoing services and may add taxes voters approved.

Levies are sorted into education, general government and bonds. Ask the district itself about a particular levy. All money goes to the Multnomah County Tax Collector.

A buyer will take over roughly this bill. Since assessed value is usually the lower number, it will not track today's sale price.

How to appeal your Portland property value

Your petition to the Property Values Appeals Board must be postmarked or delivered by December 31, and a meter stamp will not do. Private citizens appointed by county commissioners sit on the board, which operates apart from the Assessor's Office.

  • $30 per account, with a separate petition for each. Mail or hand delivery only.
  • The burden is on you to show the assessor's value exceeds market value on January 1.
  • Acceptable evidence: a sale between unrelated parties near January 1, a fee appraisal, or comparable sales adjusted for differences.
  • Hearings take about 15 minutes at the Multnomah Building, between the first Monday in February and April 15.

You hear the decision the day of your hearing, and the written order typically follows within a week, with any refund mailed afterward. Disagree? Oregon Tax Court is next, and the order tells you how to get there.

When Portland property tax goes unpaid

A delinquent balance gains 1.3333% a month after each 15th. The lien attaches July 1, when a new July to June tax year begins. Three years after the earliest delinquency, real property can be foreclosed.

By the county's own example, 2021 taxes delinquent May 16, 2022 could be foreclosed in May 2025. Owners facing foreclosure receive mailed notices laying out each step and payment deadline.

The oldest tax is always paid first. To stay out of escalated collection, ask for a payment plan on the county's delinquent tax request form or phone Tax Collections at 503-988-3334. Once judgment is entered, the county holds the property for two years while it can still be redeemed.

A simple sequence for a Portland seller

  1. Open your latest statement and find out whether it is a yellow one sent at a lender's request.
  2. Phone customer service at 503-988-2225 and ask what has been paid and what is still owed.
  3. If the value looks too high, collect a sale, appraisal or comparable sales near January 1, and file before December 31.
  4. If back years are open, ask Tax Collections about a payment plan before foreclosure notices arrive.
  5. Give the title company the statement, any lien notices and the payoff figure, so closing runs without surprises.

A cash sale of a house as it stands skips repair negotiations and lender appraisals, which can shorten this list considerably for an inherited or neglected property.

Selling a Portland house with tax due

Escrow or the title company gets a payoff figure from the county and settles unpaid tax from your proceeds. A deed recorded in Multnomah County costs $86 for page one and $5 per extra page, a charge you will see on the closing statement.

Inherited a Portland house, or own one with back taxes? Find out what the county says you owe before listing, and keep an eye on the three-year foreclosure clock. Our offers are for houses as they stand, so the roof and the yard can wait. Send the address and any tax notices to us.

Frequently asked questions

Who do I pay Portland property tax to?

The Multnomah County Tax Collector, in person at Suite 175 of 501 SE Hawthorne Blvd or online at proptax.multco.us. If your Portland house is in a Clackamas or Washington County sliver, that county bills you.

When is Portland property tax due in 2026?

The first payment is due November 16, 2026. Full payment by that day saves 3% and two-thirds saves 2%. Installment payers owe again on February 16, 2027 and May 17, 2027.

How do I appeal my Portland property value?

Mail or deliver a petition and the $30 per-account fee to the Property Values Appeals Board by December 31. Cases are heard from the first Monday in February to April 15.

What interest rate applies to late property tax in Multnomah County?

1.3333% a month, charged after each 15th. Three years of delinquency opens the door to foreclosure.

Can I sell my Portland house if I owe property tax?

Yes. Closing normally clears the tax from your proceeds, and either the county or your title company will quote a payoff.
